ROLE: Close an owned descriptor once and mark it invalid, so any later cleanup cannot close the same descriptor twice (or close an unrelated descriptor that reused the number).

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: close
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 on success, -1 with errno set (EINTR or EIO on a pathological send-side failure)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the descriptor is released whether or not close reports an error
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: the return value is deliberately ignored: after close the descriptor number is no longer usable, so retrying could close a descriptor that an accept reused; the caller only records the outcome for logging

LOGIC.INPUT: fd: pointer to a descriptor slot owned by the caller (a session field or a local in main/loop).
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If fd is NULL return. 2) If *fd < 0 return (idempotent no-op: the slot is already invalid). 3) close(*fd) and ignore the return value; save errno only if diagnostics are wanted. 4) *fd = -1 unconditionally, so the slot can be passed here again without closing a recycled descriptor number. 5) Return. This is the single place where the broker releases descriptors, so the ownership sequence is uniform: net_listen returns one descriptor to main, net_accept hands each peer descriptor to a session through broker_accept/session_create, and every release (session teardown, immediate close after a protocol error, loop shutdown, main cleanup, listener teardown) goes through this function.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: No return value. After the call *fd is -1 and the underlying descriptor, if any, was closed exactly once. A slot that is already -1 is left at -1.
INVARIANTS_USED: each descriptor is owned by exactly one slot and closed exactly once
clearing a slot's numeric value after closing prevents a double close of a recycled descriptor number
releasing a session must never affect another session's descriptor
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: fd is NULL or points to an int slot holding either -1 or a descriptor this caller owns.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: *fd == -1 and no descriptor owned by the previous value remains open (or none existed).
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Safe for distinct slots; a slot must not be closed concurrently by two threads.

EXPECT.note: a repeated cleanup path cannot close a reused descriptor number
